info.title: WeaveSignal control plane API
info.description: The station's HTTP API, `/api/v1` (ADR-0195). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only. Bodies are JSON. The narrative (authorisation, errors, stability) is in the product documentation's *Control plane routes* page.

post.description: Stops the grace for the handover now at the post (the next show's, as `post` in `GET /studio` names it): the schedule never takes the air from whoever holds it, and the handover is by a press only. It holds this handover alone; the next one is not held. For an admin or a producer; an API token never. 409 when there is no handover to hold.

delete.description: Lets the held handover go: the grace runs again, counted from where the post and the next host's standing by put it (a grace that was already over hands over at the next look). For an admin or a producer.

get.description: Open: what the public pages show anyway. The accent colour and the addresses of the brand icon and the banner, each `null` until set. A station without a database answers with all three `null`.

put.description: Admin only. One sRGB colour as six hex digits. The pages derive each theme's accent from it (its lightness moved until it reads at 4.5:1), so any colour is accepted. Empty goes back to the product's own.

200.description: The look as it is now.

get.description: Open. The PNG the station made from the upload. Under the version its address carries (`?v=`, from `GET /api/v1/branding`) it may be kept for good; `404` when the station has set none.

put.description: Admin only. The body is the picture itself, a PNG or a JPEG (recognised by its first bytes; nothing else is read, and never SVG). At most 4 MB, at least 600 by 200 pixels; it is cropped about its middle to three to one and fitted inside 1,200 by 400. The station stores and serves the PNG its media worker writes, never the upload, so no metadata survives.

200.description: The look as it is now.

413.description: The body is larger than this picture may be.

delete.description: Admin only. The pages go back to the product's own.

200.description: The look as it is now.

get.description: Open. The PNG the station made from the upload. Under the version its address carries (`?v=`, from `GET /api/v1/branding`) it may be kept for good; `404` when the station has set none.

put.description: Admin only. The body is the picture itself, a PNG or a JPEG (recognised by its first bytes; nothing else is read, and never SVG). At most 1 MB, each side 64 to 4,096 pixels; it is fitted inside 256 pixels square with its transparency kept. The station stores and serves the PNG its media worker writes, never the upload, so no metadata survives.

200.description: The look as it is now.

413.description: The body is larger than this picture may be.

delete.description: Admin only. The pages go back to the product's own.

200.description: The look as it is now.

post.description: A listener's call from the player page, with their consent to record (the words from `GET /api/v1/player`) and the answered challenge. Answers with a pass and a room token for the caller's booth. 409 (`field` `consent`) when the words have changed since the page loaded; 429 over the per-address limit.

429.description: Too many calls from this address just now.

500.description: The token could not be signed.

get.summary: A challenge to answer before calling
get.description: A proof-of-work challenge (ADR-0006); harder while the station is busy. Never cached.

post.description: A card from the fields in the body (`station` filled in when left out), as a PNG; nothing is kept.

500.description: The database or the card renderer failed.

post.description: The same fields, checked as the preview checks them (a refused name is refused here too): the alt text, the page the card links to, the level and the station fields. Nothing is drawn.

500.description: The database or the card renderer failed.

get.description: The station's banks and carts, which every show shares, and with `show` that show's own beside them (each owner's banks are numbered 1 to 5 apart; a bank or cart names its show, or `null` for the station's). A studio window asks for its show: a live window the show the station's step comes from, a preparing window the show it prepares. Each cart with FILE MISSING. Fetch it again when the studio view's `carts.version` moves.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description:
A show's slug: its own banks and carts come beside the station's. Left out, the
station's alone.

put.summary: Put an audio file in a station slot
put.description: An audio file as the body, the cart's words in the query. The media worker reads it in its sandbox, brings it to the station's loudness and makes it the cart in that slot of the station's bank.

requestBody.description: The audio file (any format the media worker reads), at most `carts.max_upload_mb`.

500.description: The cart wall failed.
The cart wall failed.

patch.description: Changes the cart in that slot of the station's bank and keeps its sound: its `label`, `detail`, `mode`, `ramp_ms` (`null` takes the ramp away) and `licence`; `bank` and `slot` move it to an empty slot of the station's banks, and the slot is its key on the wall. A field left out stays as it is. The cart keeps its id and its file, so one that is sounding goes on sounding. An empty slot is 404; a move onto a slot that holds a cart is 409, and so nothing is ever replaced by a move. To change the sound, `PUT` a file to the slot.

200.description: The cart as it is now.

500.description: The cart wall failed.

put.summary: Make or rename a station bank
put.description: A bank of the station's, shared by every show. A show's own banks are `/api/v1/shows/{show}/carts/banks/{number}`. Answers with the station's catalogue.

500.description: The cart wall failed.

post.summary: Fire, stop or cue a cart
post.description: `toggle`, `fire`, `stop`, `cue` a cart; `stop_last`; `fade_all`; `clear_cue`. Carts sound in the desk (ADR-0117). A cart in a show's own bank starts only while that show is the one the station's step comes from (409 otherwise); anything sounding can be stopped. Answers with the new studio view.

500.description: The cart wall failed.

get.description: The pack the station loaded into its banks at its first start (`carts.demo_pack`): its banks with each sound's slot, name and mode, and `untouched`, the ids of the station's carts that are still a default pack's cart as it was loaded (the same name, slot and mode, nothing added), which a load with `replace` may replace or remove. `available` is false, with `problem`, on a station that has no pack.

post.summary: Load the default pack into station banks
post.description: Loads banks of the station's default pack into station banks: each of `loads` names one of the pack's banks and the station bank it goes `into` (made, under the pack's name, if it has not been). A station bank that holds carts is refused (409, saying what would happen) unless `replace` is true. With `replace`, only default carts nobody changed are replaced, and those the pack has no sound for are removed; a cart a person added, renamed, moved or changed stays, and the pack's sound for its slot is left out. Answers 202 at once with the plan: the sounds then go through the media worker one by one, counted in the studio view's `carts.importing`. A second load while one runs is 409. As the slots' own routes: any member of staff, or a token with `carts:write`.

A chat mode (`slow`, `hold_new`, `links_trusted`) on or off, or influx (five settings at once, the earlier ones back when turned off, ADR-0068). The studio's modes; the chat service reads them. Answers with the new studio view.

The same requests as the desk's control socket, without `status`: `on_air`, `mute`, `cue`, `talk`, `talk_to`, or `dump` the profanity delay. Answers with the new studio view. A caller cannot go on air or in cue without their consent to record on file (409). The show on air's step switches some off (409, ADR-0271): `dump` below `callers`, the handover (the next DJ going on air) and `picture` below `full`, where the picture is held on the slate.

get.summary: Whether the front page is the not-set-up page
get.description: Open. For the Cloudron package's nginx, which serves the pages itself: its `/` on the app's own domain asks this route and, on a 200, serves the page named in `X-Accel-Redirect` (the not-set-up page) instead of the player. 200 while setup is open and the station still has a name nobody chose: the one its install gave it (`This station`) or the demo's (`Kettle FM`, what installs before 1.1 started as); 404 otherwise. The public pages' domain never asks, and never passes this route. The same rule decides `/` on a station whose control plane serves the pages itself.

200.description: The station is not set up: serve the not-set-up page.

X-Accel-Redirect.description: The page to serve in place of the player.

404.description: The station is set up, or is running as it was: the player stays.

get.summary: The programme sent to another Icecast server
get.description: ADR-0226: whether the station sends its programme, as an Icecast source, to a server of the deployment's choosing (a DJ's AzuraCast). Says whether it is set up, the station's choice (`auto`, `on`, `off`), whether it is sending now and why, whether the remote server took the login, the last error in words, and bytes sent. The server's password is never in the answer. Any signed-in staff may read it.

put.summary: Choose when the programme is sent to another Icecast server
put.description: Admin only. The choice is kept across restarts. It takes effect at once. The server's address, user and password are the deployment's settings (`ICECAST_OUT_*`), not this route's.

200.description: The outgoing source after the change.

500.description: The database refused.

post.description: For the ingest on this machine only, before it reads any media. With the key id (and, for Icecast, the secret; for a pull, way `pull` and no secret) and the address: `standby` with the desk slot promised to it, `test` (outside its slot, never on the desk) with how long, or `refused` with its reason. For SRT the reply carries the passphrase for the handshake; the handshake's outcome comes back on `events`. Five wrong keys from a public address in a minute refuse it for ten minutes; an address that is private, loopback, link-local or carrier-grade NAT is counted and logged but never refused.

get.description: For the ingest on this machine only (a loopback peer, no proxy's header, the bearer in `WEAVESIGNAL_INGEST_TOKEN`): whether to listen, and on which ports; and the pulls to hold open now (each pull whose slot's door is open). The ingest asks every few seconds.

post.description: For the ingest on this machine only: a connection admitted (after SRT's handshake), a test begun, a refusal the ingest made (a failed SRT handshake counts as a wrong key; a format it cannot read; a key in use; too fast), or an end. Written to the key's log.

For the ingest on this machine only, every second: what it holds. The reply names the connections to close, and those standing by whose slot's door has closed and that are not on air, which become private tests (their time running from then; one on air is never touched).

A link for a guest, a remote DJ or a presenter. A caller joins another way (422). The show on air's step decides which seats can be invited (ADR-0271): below `guests` a guest or a second presenter is refused, below `full` a DJ is, each with 422 and `field` `role`; the pass is checked again when it is used. With `for_me` the invitation is a presenter's for the signed-in account, allowed at every step for the show's presenter (403 for another account at Solo, 422 for the station key); it is the Solo DJ's own microphone link.

get.description: VBAN in (each bound to a show key) and out, the address they use, the preset, and whether this installation may use VBAN at all (never on Cloudron; elsewhere only with `[kit] vban = true` in the settings file). Admin only.

put.description: The whole kit at once, checked: at most four VBAN ins and four outs; a named address of the station's, refused when public unless `allow_public`; each input a sender's address and stream name bound to a show key; each output one receiver (never broadcast or multicast). The ingest listens afresh and the desk sends afresh within seconds. 409 when the kit asks for VBAN and this installation does not allow it. Admin only.

get.summary: One clock: each source against the desk's
get.description: For the clock badge: every host's own studio at the desk with its clock against the desk's in ppm (the desk resamples it once to follow it), the times it was placed afresh, VBAN's lost and dropped packets, and VBAN out's counts. Any staff member.

post.description: A radio preset's routing in one press: `studio_lan` sends the live programme (before the delay) back to the studio PC; `transmitter` sends the programme after the delay, what listeners hear; `local_guest` sends the first VBAN in's sender the monitor mix the desk makes for it; `custom` changes nothing but the name. VBAN ins are kept (each needs its show key). Checked and saved as `PUT` is. Admin only.

500.description: The database refused.

put.summary: Add a track to the library
put.description: An audio file as the body, the track's words in the query: the media worker normalises it into the library.

500.description: The media worker or the library failed.
The database refused.

get.description: The recordings, and the hours of the last day with none while the logger was on.

What the host behind a monitor link sees: their own source's state (`on_air`, `open`, `standby`, `link_lost`, `test`, `not_connected`) and the lamp's sentence, what happens next with the instant it counts to (`then.at_ms`, on the station's clock), the post (the grace, a hold, the late count) as far as it is theirs, before you, you and after you, the next insert as far as the log can say, the show's step, the next host, the last refusal in words, what the station hears of them, and what they may press now (`controls`, each with `why_not`). The bearer is the monitor secret from the key's making; it needs no account. 401 for a secret that is not one; 410 when the key has ended; 429 for too many wrong secrets from one address.

post.description: Puts the next host (`next_host` in the view: the show after this one's host standing by, or the DJ in the room waiting) in this host's headphones, or takes them out (`{"on": false}`). The body may be empty. The desk's own cue, for the one person the station works out: no identity is taken from the request. Refused (409) unless this host is on air and the next is at the desk and not on air.

Throws away what the profanity delay holds (the desk's own Dump, on every outgoing stream), for the host who is on air. `lost_ms` is how much of the programme listeners lost. Refused (409, with the words) unless this host is on air and the show's step has Dump (Callers and up). The page asks for two presses within three seconds; nothing here counts them.

The desk's End show (`POST /api/v1/show/end`), scoped to this host. With nobody else presenting it is the whole of it: everyone on air comes off, the carts fade, and the air passes to the next host standing by (`passed_to`) or goes to automation once the profanity delay has played out (`automation_in_ms`). With another presenter on air, only this host leaves and that presenter keeps the air. Refused (409) unless this host is on air. The page asks once first; `controls.end_show_says` is what it says follows.

get.summary: The monitor link's view, as events
get.description: Server-sent events: a `view` event whose data is the same JSON as `GET /api/v1/monitor`, at once and then every second (its `station.now_ms` is the station's clock, for the page's counts); a keep-alive comment every 10 seconds. When the key ends the stream says `ended` (its data: `{"error": "This link no longer works. Ask the station for a new one."}`) and closes. The bearer is the monitor secret, in the `Authorization` header (never in the address). Up to six streams a link; a seventh is refused with 429.

post.description: The host's own press: skips the late count, or takes the air at the show's time. It is the desk's own Go on air now (`POST /api/v1/sources/{key}/go`), for this host's source only. Refused (409, with the words) unless the source is standing by and steady, the show's time has come, and nobody else presents. The bearer is the monitor secret.

`{"step": "bring"}` puts the next host on air beside this one (the overlap); `{"step": "hand_over"}` then takes this host (and anyone else presenting) off air, so the next holds it. The two presses of the desk's own handover (ADR-0231), for the one next host the station works out. Refused (409, with the words) unless this host is on air, the show runs at Full, the next is at the desk, and (for the second) the first press has been made.

post.summary: Not yet: stop the late count
post.description: Stops the late count for this host's airing: the schedule will not put them on air by itself, and they go on air by their own press (`go`). The desk's own Not yet (`POST /api/v1/sources/{key}/not-yet`), for this host's source only. Refused (409) unless their count is running.

post.summary: A room token for the monitor link
post.description: A 600 s listen-only token for the host's monitor room, where the desk publishes the programme without them, the cue bus and talk addressed to them (ADR-0118: only the link's two seats may subscribe). Two browsers may listen at once: a third is refused with 409. The bearer is the monitor secret. 410 when the key has ended; 503 when the room is not set up.

500.description: The token could not be signed.

get.description: What listeners are told is playing, offset by the listener delay. Never what comes next for a US statutory webcaster.

get.summary: What is playing now, as events
get.description: Server-sent events: a `now_playing` event whose data is the same JSON as `GET /api/v1/now-playing`, at once and on every change.
This document: the API as OpenAPI 3.1, generated from the handlers. Needs no bearer; the description is not secret.

The pass is the bearer: from an invitation's link or a call-in. Says who it is for and whether the studio has ended it. `not_now` says why the pass cannot join yet when the show on air runs at a step that has switched its seat off (ADR-0271); the pass stays good for later.

410.description: This link has expired. Ask the station for a new one.

get.description: Server-sent events: a `me` event whose data is the person's state as JSON, at once and when it changes; a keep-alive every 10 seconds.

410.description: This link has expired. Ask the station for a new one.

post.description: A caller's call ends: out of the queue and the room, no held place. For anyone else it does nothing.

410.description: This link has expired. Ask the station for a new one.

post.summary: A room token for a pass
post.description: Signs a token for the person's room: a caller's booth, or the studio. 410 when the studio has ended the pass or no longer has the call on file, or when the lines have closed on a caller. 409 when the show on air runs at a step that has switched this seat off (ADR-0271): the sentence says so, and the pass stays good for later. Someone already in the room is never refused.

410.description: This link has expired, or the studio has ended it.

500.description: The token could not be signed.

post.description: Off air and out of the cue, the pass refused from now on (across a restart), then out of the room (ADR-0119). Someone not in the room yet (a leaked link nobody has used) is ended all the same.

502.description: Their pass is ended and they are off air, but LiveKit did not remove them.

get.description: Admin only. The remembered guests and hosts, by name.

500.description: The database or the card renderer failed.

post.description: Admin only. At their request (ADR-0122): their record, their name in every list and in what aired, the cards drawn again, the corrections log redacted.

500.description: The database or the card renderer failed.

get.description: Whether the line takes calls and why not, the calls at the gate and in the queue, the words a caller hears first, and whether the line's trunk and dispatch rule are made in LiveKit (`trunk`). For staff.
Every number ban that has not lapsed: its ban key, the last digits as the screener saw them, the day and the reason. Never a number. For staff.

post.description: Ban a phone caller in the queue by `identity` (staff), or a number by `number` (an admin; every form it may arrive in is banned). The station keeps the ban key and the last digits, never the number. A withheld caller cannot be banned by number (409: "Cannot ban a withheld number"). Caller ID can be spoofed: a ban is advisory.

delete.description: Lift the ban with this ban key. An admin's.

put.summary: Change whether the consent words play, and which shipped voice
put.description: Change `consent_words` (play the words before a caller joins the queue) or `default_voice` (`alba`, `edinburgh` or `own`: which shipped recording plays until the station records its own), or both; a field left out stays as it is. Each wins over the installation's setting (`PHONE_CONSENT_WORDS`, `PHONE_DEFAULT_VOICE`) from the next call, and is kept in the database. The station's own recording, once made, plays instead of either voice; `own` with no recording closes the line while the words are on. An admin's.

200.description: The line with its new settings.

get.description: One of the two recordings of the phone words that ship with WeaveSignal, for the studio's Play: `alba.opus` (a Scottish woman, the default) or `edinburgh.opus` (a man from Edinburgh), Ogg Opus, CC BY 4.0 (NOTICES.md). For staff.

post.description: The consent records of the calls a number may have made, found by its ban keys (every form the number may have arrived in). The number is used for this request only. A withheld call cannot be found by number: find it by its date, time and show. An admin's.

put.summary: Keep the station's recording of the phone words
put.description: The body is the recording, in any format the media worker reads (at most 8 MB, 1.5 s to 2 minutes). It must say `words_to_record` from `GET /api/v1/phone`; the station keeps those words beside it, and the line closes when they change until the words are recorded again. It replaces the recording before, and takes the place of the shipped default. An admin's.

200.description: The line with its new words.

delete.summary: Remove the station's recording of the phone words
delete.description: The shipped default plays again. An admin's.

200.description: The line with the default words.

get.description: The station, the show, the stream, whether the presenter is live, whether call-in is open (and the consent words), and the HLS addresses while the desk has video on.
Mode, what is on air, dead air, whether the default loop plays (ADR-0130), automation's queue, listeners, the logger and now playing.

post.summary: Hand the air to automation, or take it back
post.description: Sets the station's mode (ADR-0045) without changing any other playout setting, and answers with the new studio view. Any staff member's: `PUT /api/v1/playout/settings` stays an admin's. Anyone on air at the desk is not taken off air; in `auto` the desk is simply not heard, and in `live` it is heard again at once. The change is immediate (profanity delay and all); End show (`POST /api/v1/show/end`) is the route that takes people off air and waits for the delay. 503 when the station has no playout layer.

500.description: The database refused.

post.description: Asks playout (Liquidsoap) to shut down so that its supervisor, which every install has (Compose's restart policy, the Quadlet's `Restart=always`, the Cloudron app's supervisord), starts it again: the studio's `⌃R` pressed twice. Listeners keep their stream: the listener process holds the mount and plays its fallback until playout is back, about five seconds. Any staff member's, as the station's mode is (it changes what is on air, so a window that is preparing a show is refused with 409); an API token never reaches it. 502 when playout does not answer on its socket (it is already down, and its supervisor is starting it); 503 when the station has no playout layer.

502.description: Playout did not answer on its socket.

get.description: Time zone, separations, US statutory licence, mode, logger days, default clock.

500.description: The database refused.

put.description: Admin only. Reading the settings is any staff member's; changing them, the US statutory licence among them, is an admin's. A zone change reaches the schedule's screens at once, and `mode` (`live` or `auto`) the studio's view and the desk.

500.description: The database refused.

get.description: The station's zone and whether anyone has chosen it (ADR-0189). The studio asks an admin to choose once, with the configuration's zone offered; any signed-in staff may read it.

For a station's own website: aired episodes with published files, newest first, with where to hear them, their card, their page and their feed. Page back with `before_ms`. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s.

parameters.name: before_ms
parameters.description: Only episodes that aired before this time (the last one's `air_at_ms`, to page back).

get.description: For a station's own website: the episodes with an air time from now for `days` days, in air order. An episode that has not aired shows as its slot (show, series, number, time, length, kind, hosts); its title, description, guests and tags appear once it has aired. No person a retention rule erased appears. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days from now, 1 to 14.

get.summary: The schedule as a calendar file
get.description: For a person's own calendar (subscribe to it, or download it): every show with a rule, as one VEVENT each (its RRULE or RDATE, EXDATE for skipped dates, an override with RECURRENCE-ID for each moved date), in the station's zone with its VTIMEZONE, so the calendar works out the dates and the clocks changing itself. A show's rule is its current series' (that series' own start date and planned episodes win). Only the public words: the show's name and its description (its page, as `URL`, once the station serves show pages); a drafted episode's title and guests are never in it. Each show's UID is `{show id}@weavesignal` and stays the same for the show's life. `text/calendar; charset=utf-8`. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s. Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

get.summary: One show as a calendar file
get.description: As `GET /api/v1/public/schedule.ics`, for one show: `{file}` is the show's path with `.ics` (`/api/v1/public/shows/the-late-kettle.ics`). A show without a rule gives a calendar with no events, so a subscription does not fail while a rule is cleared. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s. Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

For a station's own website: the station, the show now, the stream, whether the show is live, whether call-in is open, the video, the zone. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 5 s.

Whether this station has a rehearsal studio, its desk's link, the open session (one show at a time), the people at the rehearsal desk and the carts sounding there. Nothing in the rehearsal studio reaches the air. `may_run` says whether the asker may run the open session. The studio app fetches it once and then follows `GET /api/v1/rehearsal/events`.

Every booking of the rehearsal studio that shares any time with the stretch asked for (at most 62 days), in start order. A booking holds the studio for its show: Open for another show is refused while one does. The rehearsal studio is first come; bookings are optional. The schedule's week also gives them, with the sessions, as `rehearsals`. For staff; an API token with `schedule:read`.

parameters.name: from_ms
parameters.description: From, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

post.description: Books the rehearsal studio for one show from `start_ms` until `end_ms`: 201 and the booking. From now on (a minute's slack), at least five minutes and at most a day (422 naming the field). Bookings never share time: one that would is 409, with the sentence and the booking in the way (`clash`); one that starts as another ends does not share time. Whoever may change the show's step may (its presenter, a producer, an admin, the station key); 403 otherwise. 503 when the station has no rehearsal studio or no database.

409.description: It would share time with another booking.

delete.description: Frees the rehearsal studio from a booking that is not over: 204. One that is over is 409, and stays in the schedule. Whoever may change the step of the booking's show (a producer or an admin included); 403 otherwise. An open session is not ended by this.

patch.description: Moves or resizes a booking, or gives it to another show; what is left out stays. The same checks as a new booking, except that a booking under way keeps its start. One that is over is 409, and stays as it was. Sharing time with another booking is 409 with `clash`. Whoever may change the step of the booking's show, and of the show it goes to; 403 otherwise.

409.description: It would share time with another booking (with `clash`), or it is over.

post.summary: A switch or a cart at the rehearsal desk
post.description: The rehearsal desk's switches (`on_air`: into the rehearsal's mix, never the air; `mute`, `cue`, `talk`, `talk_to`) and its carts (`cart_fire`, `cart_stop`, `cart_stop_all`). Nothing else: any other op, `dump` and `picture` among them, is 422 naming it. These never reach the live desk. A cart fires from the rehearsed show's own banks or the station's, whatever show is on air; another show's is 409, and its plays are not in the per-play log. Whoever may run the session's show (403 otherwise), from a live or a preparing window. 409 with no session open. Answers with the rehearsal view.

200.description: The rehearsal view after the command.

post.description: Ends the open session: its rehearsal links buy nothing from now on, every cart at the rehearsal desk fades, and everyone is taken out of the rehearsal room. Whoever may run the session's show (403 otherwise), from a live or a preparing window; 409 with no session open. Answers with the rehearsal view.

200.description: The rehearsal view, with no session.

post.description: WHIP (RFC 9725) for a host's own software (17d): the body is an SDP offer (`application/sdp`) and the bearer is the show key's secret (OBS's *Bearer Token*; `<key id>-<secret>` is taken too). The reply is `201` with the SDP answer and the session's address in `Location`. The station answers ICE-lite with one host candidate, its public IPv4 address and its WHIP port (`ports.source_whip`, UDP, off unless the installation turns it on), and takes the Opus sound only: a picture the software sends is received and discarded, so OBS needs no change. From there the source is a host's own studio like Icecast and SRT (ADR-0280): standing by in its show's slot, a private test outside it, refused with a wrong key (five wrong keys from an address in a minute refuse it for ten minutes). No trickle ICE.

only in the reply that makes the key.

host.description:
The station's address as listeners reach it, when the settings give one; else the
studio fills in the address it knows.

oneOf.description: For a pull: the address the station opens, and how.

Drafted.description: What to do with the episodes drafted for dates to come when a rule changes.

Dumped.description: A Dump just taken, for the host who was on air (design sections 3.7 and 8).

at_ms.description: When it was taken, on the station's clock.

lost_ms.description: What listeners lost, in milliseconds: what the delay held.

seconds.description: The same in whole seconds, as the words say it.

words.description: What the page says: *Dumped. Listeners lost 8 s. Carry on, and do not repeat the words.*

EdgeHealth.description: What the control plane knows of one edge's health.

last_error.description: The last failure's reason, cleared by a pass.

last_ms.description: How long the last check took, in milliseconds.

since.description: When `up` last changed (or the control plane started).

up.description: In the order: checked and passing, or never checked.

first.description: Manifests since the control plane started that put this edge first.

force.description: Accept a break of the station's own separations (never of the US statutory licence).

oneOf.description: Up to and including this date (the station's local date of the start).
After this many episodes: a skipped date does not count.

EndShowResult.description: What End show did, and the view after it.

automation_in_ms.description:
When the air goes to automation: `0` it already was there; a number of milliseconds is
how long until the profanity delay has played out (the goodbye is not cut off) and the
station is switched; `null` this station has no playout layer to hand the air to, so
everyone is off air and nothing more happened.

off_air.description: How many people and sources were taken off air.

passed_to.description:
The next host's name when they were standing by and the air passed to them (with
`automation_in_ms` null: nothing went to automation); absent otherwise.

view.description: The new studio view, as every command answers.

occurrence.description:
The rule date this episode fills, as the station's local date of the nominal start.
Drafting sets it and dragging the episode keeps it (that makes the block MOVED); an
episode made or left by hand has none.

EpisodeAt.description: An episode that stays where it is, and the date it holds.

on.description: The rule date it fills, if it fills one.

EpisodeKind.description:
Whether an episode is broadcast live or played from a recording (ADR-0188). Studios, the
other half of that decision, are not modelled yet.

EpisodePatch.description: A change to an episode. An inheriting field set to `null` goes back to inheriting.

oneOf.description: Live or pre-recorded (ADR-0188); it has no level above to inherit from.

EpisodeRef.description: An episode named in an erasure's answer.

card_files_deleted.description: Card files that named them, deleted.

cards_not_redrawn.description: Cards that could not be drawn again (cards are off: no public address): still old.

cards_redrawn.description: Cards drawn again without the name.

corrections_redacted.description: Lines of the corrections log that held the name, redacted (ADR-0177).

files.description: Published audio files whose tags may still name them: to be published again.

mentions.description: Episodes whose title or description still names them: for a person to edit.

reason.description: Why it has to be kept longer.

until_ms.description: The new date to keep it until, in milliseconds since the epoch.

File.description: A file as the whole body: audio to normalise, a picture.

enclosure.description: The MP3 or AAC file (ADR-0018), as named in `publishing.episodes_dir`.

Floor.description: The least a rule requires, in days, and the rule.

condition.description:
When the floor applies, where it applies only in some cases (ADR-0155); `None` when it
always does.

gaps.description: What could not be filled, in words.

items.description: How many items the log now holds for the span.

GpuFacts.description:
A graphics card the desk could encode the station's video on (NVENC), as the install knows it
(1.2.1, ADR-0292): that a card is there, not its model, so not whether it has the AV1
encoder the station's video needs (the desk falls back to the CPU where it has not). The studio's Settings offers a card that is there and not in use; nothing
turns one on but the settings file's `GPU=nvidia`, set by a person, and an update never does.

found.description:
Whether the install script found an NVIDIA card on this server that the desk could be
handed (its CDI spec, looked for by `weavesignal.sh` on every run). Always false on the
Cloudron package, whose apps are given no card.

in_use.description:
Whether the desk has been handed the card (`GPU=nvidia`): the setting, not a reading of
the desk. With video on it then encodes on the card what the card takes, and the rest on
the CPU; the desk's log says which.

video.description: Whether video is on (`VIDEO=true`): a card encodes nothing without it.

HandoverLate.description:
A host who never came (1.2.1): the show under way is theirs, nobody of theirs has taken the
air since it started, and the window is already about the next show.

host.description:
Who is down for it, by name: the source the post's rule names, else the furthest of its
hosts, else every name down for it.

state.description: How far they have got: `not_connected`, `connecting` or `ready` (standing by, not on air).

HandoverReadiness.description: How ready the incoming host is.

step.description:
`bring`: the first press, the next host on air beside this one (the overlap). `hand_over`:
the second, everyone else presenting comes off air and the next holds it.

HandoverWindow.description: The handover window as `GET /studio` and `GET /sources` carry it, inside `post`.

heads_up_ms.description: When the incoming host was given their heads-up for this airing (once an airing).

host.description: Who is down for it, by name: the source the post's rule names, else every name down.

oneOf.description:
The host the show under way still waits for, once the window has moved on to the next
show (1.2.1): the desk then names both, the late one first. `null` when nobody is late,
and while the window is still about the show under way (the post's own reading says it).

opens_ms.description: When the window opens (`start_ms` less the rules' `window_s`).

rehearsing.description:
The show is in the rehearsal studio now (1.3): the post line says "… rehearsing". Its
people are moved to the live studio by a press there, never by the window.

show.description:
The show it is about: the post's show (`post.show`), or the next show once that one's
window has opened while the post's show is still waiting for a host who never came.

state.description:
`quiet` (before the window opens), `announced` (not here yet), `cueing` (connecting),
`ready`, `overrun` (the post has come and the outgoing host still presents) or `held`.

HandoverWindowState.description: What the handover window is doing at `now_s`.

HeadsUpLine.description: The station's one line to the incoming host before their post.

extended_until_ms.description:
The date its latest extension fixed, which replaces the date the complaint rule gives
(ADR-0156), and who extended it, when and why.

recordings.description: What it keeps now: recordings not yet deleted, and consents.

HoldTarget.description: What a hold can name one by one in this release.

HostFrom.description: Where a show's host comes from, for the Studios view's *Own studio* chip.

HostOrigin.description: Where a show's host comes from.

mount.description: Any mount is taken; this one is suggested.

password.description: The key id and the secret, joined by a hyphen.

user.description: Any user name is taken; most software insists on one.

mode.description:
`auto`: send while the station is live with the desk on air. `on`: send whatever
listeners hear, until turned off. `off`: never.

IcecastOutMode.description:
Whether the programme is sent to another Icecast server (ADR-0226).

The server's address and password are the deployment's settings; this is the one choice made
while the station runs.

IcecastOutStatus.description:
The outgoing Icecast source (ADR-0226): the programme sent to another Icecast server as a
source, for a DJ's AzuraCast. The listener process holds the connection and says how it is
doing (`icecast_out.status`); the control plane decides when it sends. The remote password
is never in here.

bytes_sent.description:
Counted from the stream's constant bit rate while connected, since the listener process
started; not read from the socket.

configured.description:
The deployment sends to a server and has its password (`ICECAST_OUT` in the settings).
Everything below is empty when it is false.

connected.description: The remote server accepted the login and takes the stream.

connected_since_ms.description: When the current connection was made, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

failures.description: Failed tries in a row; the pause between tries grows from 5 s to 30 s.

last_error.description: The last error, in words; kept after a reconnect, with its time. Empty if none yet.

mode.description: The station's choice: `auto` (while live with the desk on air), `on` or `off`.

reason.description: Why, in words: "live with the desk on air", "off", and so on.

wanted.description: The control plane is asking the listener process to send now.

ImportAlready.description: A show the station already has.

ImportChoice.description: A show to make, as the person chose it from the preview.

description.description: The preview's `description`, or another (at most 4,000 characters).

name.description: The show's name: the preview's, or as the person renamed it (1 to 160 characters).

rule.description: The preview's `rule`, as it came (or changed: it is checked as any rule is).

oneOf.description:
The show the station already has that this is: the same name (case and spaces folded)
and the same dates and times still to come, as the station's own calendar file gives
them. `null` for a show the station does not have. The studio leaves such a show
unticked: made again, it would be a second show at the same times.

clash_count.description:
How many of `dates` clash with a show the station has. A show that is `already` on the
station does not clash with itself: its own times are in neither `clashes` nor this.

dates.description:
Its next dates that air (and the skipped ones among them, marked), with the other shows'
times each overlaps, as the rule preview gives them.

more.description: There are more dates than those shown.

overlaps.description:
The other items of this file (by their place in `items`, from 0) whose dates overlap
this one's in the twelve months from its first date to come.

slug.description:
The path the show would take if made now with this name (`null` when refused). The
import makes the path free again when it makes the show, so a renamed show takes its
new name's.

oneOf.description: The rule's sentence, short form and last date (`null` when refused).

ImportItem.description: One show the file proposes, with what the New show preview says of a rule.

notes.description: About the file as a whole: cancelled events left out, changed dates that match nothing.

ready.description: How many items can be made (those not refused).

zone.description: The station's zone: every time is on its clock.

ImportPreviewRequest.description:
A calendar file to read, as JSON. The route also takes the file itself, sent as
`text/calendar`.

ics.description: The file's text (iCalendar, UTF-8): at most 1 MB and 200 events.

limit.description: How many dates that air to show for each proposed show: 1 to 20, five by default.

made.description: The shows made, in the order sent, each with its path, rule, sentence and next date.

warnings.description:
The made shows whose dates overlap another show's time, the others made in the same
import included.

ImportWarning.description: A made show that overlaps another show's time.

clashes.description:
Its dates in the twelve months from its first (the first 60) that overlap another
show's time, one entry per overlap.

show.description: The made show's path and name.

IngestConfig.description: What the ingest needs to listen.

listen.description: Whether to listen at all: only once a key exists that has not ended.

port_bridge.description: The bridge's WebSocket, on loopback behind the proxy (Phase 17g); 0: off.

port_icecast.description: 0: this way is off (the installation turned it off).

port_whip.description: WHIP's media port (UDP); 0: this way is off.

pulls.description:
The pulls to hold open now: every pull whose slot's door is open and that is not turned
away. The ingest opens those it does not hold and closes those no longer named.

test_max_ms.description: A test's longest life, in ms.

oneOf.description: VBAN in (Phase 17g): where to listen and the bindings; `None`: not at all.

IngestConn.description: A connection as the ingest reports it.

format.description:
What the host's software sends, as the ingest read it (`mp3 44.1 kHz stereo`); empty
until the first sound is decoded.

kbps.description: What arrives, in kbit/s, over the last few seconds.

level_db.description: Its level, dBFS RMS over the last few seconds, as decoded; `None` while silent.

lost.description:
VBAN: packets lost on the way since it opened and filled with silence (the clock
readout's `lost`); absent for every other way.

mode.description: `standby` (on the desk) or `test` (never on the desk).

since_ms.description: When the connection was taken, on the station's clock.

title.description: What the host's software says is playing (Icecast's metadata), cleaned and cut.

way.description:
`icecast`, `srt`, `whip`, `bridge` or `vban` (the host's software connected), or `pull` (the
station opened it).

connections.description: Every connection the ingest holds now, standing by or in a test.

vban_dropped.description: VBAN packets dropped since the ingest started, by reason (Phase 17g).

IngestVban.description: What the ingest needs for VBAN in: `None` when it should not listen.

Insert.description: The station's next insert, as far as the log can say (ADR-0045).

plays.description:
Whether it plays over a live show or instead of it is not in the log's model: always
`unknown` today.

InstallFacts.description:
What the page explains but cannot change: the install's own settings, as this control plane
was started with them.

gpu.description: A graphics card for the desk's video (1.2.1).

listed.description: Whether search engines may list the public pages.

mail.description: How sign-in codes go out: `command`, `outbox` or `off`.

public_url.description: The address cards and feeds print; empty on a station for this machine only.

stream_url.description: The listener stream as the player is given it.

link.description:
The join page with the pass in the fragment, which browsers never send: absolute on the
station's public address (`publishing.public_url`) when it is set, else a path.

for_me.description:
A presenter's invitation for the signed-in account itself (ADR-0274): the Solo DJ's own
microphone link, allowed at every step for the show's presenter. The name is the
account's unless one is given, and the identity is the account's own, so the same link
can be made again. Needs a staff session, not the station key.

oneOf.description: `guest`, `dj` or `presenter`. Left out only with `for_me`, where it is `presenter`.

show.description: The show to rehearse, by its slug: needed with `studio` `rehearsal`, and only then.

studio.description:
Which studio the link leads to (1.3): `live` (the default) or `rehearsal`, the
rehearsal studio for `show`, whose session must be open. A rehearsal link follows that
show's step, not the show on air's, and buys nothing once its session has ended.

ttl_s.description: Seconds; the station's `join.invite_ttl_s` when left out, and never more.

Joined.description: What a person gets to join: a room token, its pass, and the one track to listen to.

hear.description:
The desk's participant that publishes this person's mix-minus: the only one to
subscribe to (every mix-minus is visible to everyone in the room).

see.description:
While the desk has video on: the desk's participant that publishes the programme
picture, the only picture to subscribe to (ADR-0028), and the page offers the camera.

source.description:
`room`, `push` (a host's own software) or `pull` (a stream the station opens): where the
show comes from.

details.description: The details without the secrets (the ports and the key id).

oneOf.description: The last refusal, if there has been one.

KeyRow.description: A key with what the studio's row shows.

Kind.description: The kinds of record a preset sets a period for (ADR-0113's list, recce 27's columns).

allow_public.description:
Allow a public address (VBAN has no authentication or encryption: carry it through
WireGuard instead).

bind.description:
The station's own address on the network VBAN uses: VBAN in listens there, VBAN out
sends from it. Needed for either.

KitView.description: The kit as the screen shows it.

allowed.description: Whether this installation may use VBAN.

warning.description: A warning to show: the address is public.

why_not.description: Why not, when it may not.

LastRefusal.description: A refusal of the host's software, in words.

LinkLostView.description: A lost link and the place kept for it.

covered.description: Whether automation has covered it already.

covers_ms.description: When automation covers it, if nobody else is on air (the rules' silence).

place_kept_until_ms.description: Until when the place is kept for it.

ListenerDelay.description:
The listener delay the surfaces show (ADR-0103, ADR-0165, ADR-0272): the parts that are read
live, and the rest as the station's setting.

What is read live is the profanity delay (the desk reports it) and what the listener process
holds of playout's feed (its own `feed.buffer_length`). What is not: the listener
process's mount holds back a fixed stretch before it serves listeners, and each listener's
player buffers on top. No marker travels in the stream (a metadata change would chain the
Ogg stream and drop the mount, AGENTS.md), so there is no measurement from the desk to a
listener's ear; `measured` says whether there is one.

basis.description:
`estimate` while `set_ms` is not 0; `measured` only when the whole path was measured
(issue 17). The same fact as `measured`, as a word a client can show.

desk_ms.description: How much the desk's profanity delay holds now (read live from the desk), to 0.1 s.

measured.description:
True only when no part of `ms` is a setting. Nothing measures the mount's hold or a
player's buffer, so it is false in this build; the app words the figure as an estimate
and names the parts that are read.

mount_hold_ms.description:
Of `set_ms`, the listener mount's own hold (fixed, 12 s; not a setting); `null` when the
station gives the older single figure (`studio.listener_delay_ms`), which cannot be
split (ADR-0289).

process_ms.description:
How much of playout's feed the listener process holds now (read live from it, to
0.1 s); `None` while it does not answer.

read_ms.description:
The part of `ms` that is read live now: `desk_ms` plus `process_ms` (the latter 0 while
the listener process does not answer).

rest_ms.description:
The rest of the path as the settings say it (the mount's fixed 12 s and
`studio.player_allowance_ms`, or the older `studio.listener_delay_ms`): the mount's own
hold, playout and a listener's player. Never read.

set_ms.description: The part of `ms` that is a setting and never read: the same as `rest_ms`.

LogItem.description: An item of the generated log.

missing_hours.description: The hours of the last day with no recording while the logger was on.

on.description: Whether the logger is on; `null` while playout does not say.

records.description: Whether the retention setting lets the logger record.

MadeKey.description: A key just made: its row, its two secrets and the details, shown this once.

as_text.description: The same as plain text, to paste into a message.

monitor_secret.description:
The monitor link's secret, 24 characters, a second secret made and ended with the key.
Shown once.

secret.description: The key's secret, 24 characters. Shown once.

Mapping.description: How a calendar's event became a show's rule.

preparing.description:
This window is preparing a show (ADR-0276): it cannot change what is on air. Always
false for the station key and API tokens.

Mode.description: A room-wide chat mode the screener switches with one key.

mode.description:
`auto`: automation holds the air and the desk never airs (the lamp says AUTO, ADR-0183).
`live`: the desk first, automation on dead air.

MonitorDone.description: What a control answers: what it did, and the host's view after it.

automation_in_ms.description:
End show: how long until automation takes the air (`0` it holds it already); absent when
nothing goes to automation (the air passed on, another presenter keeps it, or there is
no playout layer).

lost_ms.description: Dump: how much of the programme listeners lost, in ms (what the delay held).

passed_to.description: End show: the next host's name when the air passed to them.

view.description: The host's view after it, as `GET /api/v1/monitor` gives it.

MonitorPost.description: The post, as far as it is this host's: the show whose post it is, and its clocks.

grace_ends_ms.description: When the grace ends and the schedule hands the air over from whoever holds it.

oneOf.description:
The handover window's heads-up, when this host is the one coming on next and the station
has given it (once an airing; design note `handover-window.md`).

held_by.description: Who holds this handover (a producer's Hold): the grace does not run.

host.description:
The host who takes the air at this post, by name, and where they have got to:
`standing_by`, `connecting`, `not_connected`, `link_lost` or `on_air`.

late_ends_ms.description: When the late count ends (this host's own count; `go` and `not_yet` act on it).

mine.description:
The post's show is this host's own: they are who takes the air (or one of their show's
hosts is).

on_air.description: Who presents now, on air, by name.

on_air_at_ms.description:
When the schedule puts this host on air by itself, from automation: at the post, or the
late count's end.

show_name.description: The show whose post it is.

MonitorToken.description: A listen-only room token for the host's monitor room.

identity.description: The seat the token is for.

ttl_s.description: Seconds the token can be used to join.

MonitorView.description: The monitor link's view: this host's own, and nothing of anyone else's.

door_closes_ms.description: When their slot's door closes, while it is open (the station's clock).

oneOf.description:
A Dump was taken in the last few seconds (from this link or from the desk) and this host
is on air: the page says DUMPED. Absent otherwise.

format.description: What their software sends, while connected.

oneOf.description: The next insert, as far as the log can say.
The last time the station refused their software, in words.

level.description:
Their level at the desk (short-term LUFS after the leveller); for a test, the ingest's
reading (dBFS RMS).

leveller_db.description: What the leveller does to bring them to the station's level, in dB.

listeners_behind_ms.description:
How far behind the programme listeners hear, in ms, for *Listeners hear you, about 23 s
behind.*

monitor_has_programme.description:
The host's monitor mix carries what listeners hear now: someone else is on air at the
desk and listeners hear the desk, not automation. False while automation (or the
fallback) holds the air, which the desk does not make, so the mix is silent but for cue
and talk addressed to the host. The page then plays the listeners' stream, a few
seconds behind, while the host stands by or is OPEN (in OPEN the room's voices are not
in it, and the page says so).

monitor_open.description: Whether their monitor mix is open at the desk (someone is listening).

oneOf.description: The next host: whoever this host would cue and bring on; absent when none is in sight.
The post, as far as it is this host's; absent when it is not.

says.description:
The lamp's sentence, in the design's words (*Standing by. The station hears you.
Listeners do not.*).

state.description:
The host's lamp: `on_air` (listeners hear them), `open` (the station and the room hear
them; listeners do not: automation holds the air, or playout is down), `standby`,
`link_lost`, `test`, or `not_connected`.

steady_ms.description: How long they have been connected, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: What happens next, in one sentence with its time; absent when nothing does.

title.description: What their software says is playing.

way.description: `icecast`, `srt`, `whip`, `bridge` or `vban`, while connected; `pull` while the station holds a pull open.

MountCount.description: How many listeners one mount of the listener process has now.

mount.description: The mount's path as the listener process names it, such as `/programme.opus`.

Move.description: A date that airs at another time.

from.description: The rule's date that is moved.

minutes.description: A length of its own for this date.

to.description: When it airs instead, on the station's wall clock (`2027-04-13T20:00:00`).

airing_start_ms.description: The airing they stand by for: its start, in ms since the Unix epoch.

moved.description: Everyone moved, by identity: each page is sent its live pass on its event stream.

opening.description: The opening state, applied when the show's host is put on air at the live desk.

Moved.description: An episode that moves to another date.

clashes.description: Where the new time overlaps another show's.

NewEpisodes.description: The new episodes' own fields; the rest is filled in or inherited.

count.description: How many to draft from the rule: one, or a whole season ("create 10 episodes").

title.description: The first one's title and guests; the rest start blank.

from_ms.description: A stretch of broadcast time: every recording and consent overlapping it is held.

reason.description: Why: the complaint or report, in a line.

hint.description:
`icecast`, `srt`, `whip`, `bridge` or `vban`: how they will send (a hint, not a lock); or
`pull`: the station opens the stream at `url` itself while the slot's door is open.

label.description: Who it is for: their name on the desk, 1 to 120 characters.

staff_id.description: The member of staff it is for, if one.

url.description:
For `pull` only: `http://` or `https://` (Icecast or any HTTP audio), a playlist ending
`.m3u8` (HLS), or `srt://host:port` with any `streamid=` (the station is the caller). No
user name, password or SRT passphrase. An address inside the station's own network is
refused unless the installation allows it.

expires_in_days.description: Days from now; left out, the token does not expire.

NextHostView.description: The next host, for Cue, Bring and Hand over.

NextOn.description: A show's next date, or why it has none.

NoNext.description: Why a show has no next date.

change.description:
For `rule.changed`: the token the saving window sent with its save (1.0.5), so that
window knows the notice for its own. Null for every other kind, and for a save sent
without one.

kind.description:
What it is about (`caller.ready`, `caller.declined`, `handover.heads_up`, ...), for the
app to pick keys.

subject.description:
The person it is about, if any (for `handover.heads_up`, the incoming host's desk
identity while they are at the desk); for `rule.changed`, the show's path (1.0.5).

NowPlaying.description: What listeners are told is playing.

next.description: What comes next; left out for a US statutory webcaster (17 U.S.C. 114(d)(2)(C)(ii)).

on_air.description:
`desk` (a live show), `automation`, `fallback`, `silence`, or `unknown` while playout is
not answering. The default loop WeaveSignal ships (ADR-0130) is told as `fallback`: to a
listener it is the station's fallback, and only the studio is told it is the default.

OpenDateOut.description: A date to draft, for the week's dotted blocks.

from.description:
Where its host comes from (1.3.1), as an episode's `from` says: `room`, or `own` (their
own studio, with a show key that has not ended).

number.description: The number the episode would take when drafting reaches this date.

series.description: The show's current series (the next one to be made is 1).

short.description: The rule in short, for a tooltip.

OpenRequest.description: The show to open the rehearsal studio for.

Opening.description:
The opening state a move carries (section 1.6): who is on and who is muted, applied when the
show's host is put on air at the live desk, never on arrival. `cue`, `talk` and `talk_to` are
momentary and are not carried; there are no levels to carry.

airing_end_ms.description:

api_token.description:
An API token (`rsa_…`, ADR-0195) from `POST /api/v1/tokens`, made by an admin for one integration with the scopes it needs. A token reaches only the routes its scopes open (each such route lists `api_token` with the scope it needs) and is never an admin: no route marked `x-admin` takes one. Each token is limited per minute (`429`). The scopes:

- `studio:read`: Read the studio's view: sources, callers (with the names and topics they gave), chat modes, notices; and follow it live.
- `desk:control`: Work the desk: on air, mute, cue, talk, and dump the profanity delay.
- `screener:control`: Work the screener: screen, send, decline and drop callers; end a pass.
- `chat:moderate`: Change the chat's modes (slow mode, hold new, links). The chat's own moderation routes are not reachable with a token.
- `carts:read`: Read the cart wall's banks and carts.
- `carts:fire`: Fire, stop and cue carts; stop the last; fade all.
- `carts:write`: Make and rename banks; load, change and empty cart slots; load the default pack.
- `schedule:read`: Read the clocks, the week, the log of what is to play, the episodes airing in a range, and the rehearsal studio's bookings.
- `schedule:write`: Change clocks, the week and the log; generate a day.
- `playout:read`: Read playout's status and zone, the logger, and the track library.
- `library:write`: Add tracks to the library and delete them.
- `reports:read`: Read the play and audience reports.
- `shows:read`: Read shows, series, episodes and corrections; read a calendar file into proposed shows.
- `shows:write`: Change shows, series and episodes; put an episode on air; correct one; publish its files; draw cards; make shows from a calendar file.
- `video:read`: Read the video slate's still and the cameras' thumbnails.
- `video:write`: Change or remove the video slate's still.
- `sources:read`: Read the hosts' own studios connected or due (ADR-0280): their state, way in, format and level; and the rota of the coming hours, who is down for each show and whether they are ready. Never a key.

ingest.description: The ingest's own bearer (`WEAVESIGNAL_INGEST_TOKEN`), taken only from a loopback peer with no proxy's header: the internal routes for hosts in their own studios (ADR-0280).

monitor.description: A monitor link's secret (ADR-0280): the second secret made with a show key, 24 characters, kept by the station only as a keyed hash; sent as a bearer by the monitor page, which reads it from the link's fragment.

pass.description: A pass (ADR-0119): the link a guest, a remote DJ, a presenter or a caller joins by; from `POST /api/v1/invites` or `POST /api/v1/call-in`.

show_key.description: A show key's secret (ADR-0284), 24 characters, as WHIP's bearer (17d; OBS's *Bearer Token*): the same secret as the Icecast password's second part and the SRT passphrase.

staff_session.description: A staff session token (`rss_…`) from `POST /api/v1/sessions`. An account's role decides which routes it reaches; routes marked admin only need the `admin` role.

station_key.description: The station key (`WEAVESIGNAL_CONTROL_ADMIN_TOKEN`): the station's own credential, with an admin's powers.
